chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Freddy Jenkins, the showboat of Ellington's band
summary: Jenkins was a neat, classy left-handed trumpeter with a big cigar who drew audiences in theatres, and may have briefly conducted Russell's band in 1936.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You also mentioned Freddy being a very sharp and fastidious dresser and...

Oh yeah, a dresser...! Oh yeah, he was neat as a pin. Oh yeah. He was something else. And that's why he was such a big man in Duke Ellington's band, he was so classy and he was a real showboat. Oh man, he was something else, sitting up on the bandstand with his left-handed trumpet. He played trumpet with the left hand, you know. And then playing... Oh, he was something. He was class personified. More people would come and ask for Freddy Jenkins than they did for Duke Ellington. Freddy was a big attraction in that band.
At the Cotton Club.

No, I'm talking about in theatres, when they played theatres. Oh, he was something. Yes, indeed, Freddy was the big attraction. And always had... He was a little-bitty guy, you know, and he was... Freddy was about the size I am right now, and I'm only 5 feet 3... But he was small like I am now. And always had a big cigar in his mouth. Great big cigar. Big fat El Producto cigar. He always had that big cigar. And he loved to talk. He was a real showboat.
Did you ever play with him at any other time?
Oh, I gigged with him a lot of times, sure. Different gigs and things, sure.
Well, Freddy Jenkins was from New York City.

Yeah, he was born here. That's how he got his hands on that stuff. He was hopping on the back of a truck, so they tell me. And I think the tailbone or something... He snapped all the fingers on the right hand. That's what I heard.
Yeah, because according to Chilton he switched to playing left-handed early in his teens.
Yeah.
He was briefly with Edgar Hayes in the Twenties, but you weren't involved in that.
I have never been involved with Edgar Hayes
except with the Blue Rhythm Band.
And then according to this, Jenkins had a brief spell conducting the Luis Russell band at Connie's Inn around 1936.
Yeah. You weren't with Russell then.
Oh, but that might have been one of Russell's bands. In '36, Russell was with Louis. In '35 to '36 Luis was with Louis. That might have been one of Russell's bands that he got together with somebody.
Yeah, in between Louis Armstrong's featured numbers it said that Jenkins did some direction of the band.
[PAUSE]
